{{Short description|American plant community ecologist}}
[[File:ETH-BIB-Hille Ris Lambers, Janneke (1972-)-Portr 18305.jpg|thumb|Janneke Hille Ris Lambers (2020)]]
'''Janneke Hille Ris Lambers''' (born 1972)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Congress |first=The Library of |title=Hille Ris Lambers, Janneke, 1972- - LC Linked Data Service: Authorities and Vocabularies {{!}} Library of Congress, from LC Linked Data Service: Authorities and Vocabularies (Library of Congress) |url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/no2001084682.html |access-date=2023-12-10 |website=id.loc.gov}}</ref> is a professor of [[Plant ecology|Plant Ecology]] at [[ETH Zurich]] in Switzerland at the Institute for Integrative Biology (IBZ) since 2020<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-03-06 |title=19 new professors appointed |url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2020/03/new-professors.html |access-date=2023-12-10 |website=ethz.ch |language=en}}</ref> and an Affiliate Full Professor at [[University of Washington]] in the United States. 

== Early life and education ==
Lambers was born in [[Wageningen]], Netherlands in 1972. She completed her academic training in the USA.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Janneke Hille Ris Lambers, Prof. Dr. – ETH MScLA |url=https://mscla.arch.ethz.ch/category/instructors/janneke-hille-ris-lambers/ |access-date=2023-12-10 |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-12-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231210181353/https://mscla.arch.ethz.ch/category/instructors/janneke-hille-ris-lambers/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> She received a Doctor of Philosophy degree from [[Duke University]] in 2001 on coexistence of [[temperate forest]] tree species, focusing on the differences among temperate tree species in seed dispersal, seed banking and density-dependent mortality and how those characteristics contribute to maintenance of diversity. Her thesis was supervised by James S. Clark. During her PhD she worked at the Coweeta Hydrologic Laboratory in western North Carolina (a [[Long Term Ecological Research Network|Long Term Research Research Network]] site - LTER).

== Career and research ==
Throughout her career Janneke has focused on the maintenance of species diversity and the impact of global environmental change on plant communities.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HRL Lab: people |url=https://faculty.washington.edu/jhrl/People.html |access-date=2023-11-28 |website=faculty.washington.edu}}</ref> She has worked on a variety of plant communities including temperate tree species,<ref>{{cite thesis |last1=Lambers |first1=Janneke Hille Ris |title=Dormancy, Dispersal, and Density-dependent Mortality: Coexistence of Temperate Forest Tree Species |date=2001 |oclc=48195834 |url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/ab54dad31a73f4c9a46f8286ab6bcadf/1 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lambers |first1=Janneke Hille Ris |last2=Clark |first2=James S |title=Effects of dispersal, shrubs, and density-dependent mortality on seed and seedling distributions in temperate forests |journal=Canadian Journal of Forest Research |date=May 2003 |volume=33 |issue=5 |pages=783–795 |doi=10.1139/x03-001 }}{{psc|date=December 2023}}</ref> grassland communities,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Borer |first1=Elizabeth T. |last2=Seabloom |first2=Eric W. |last3=Gruner |first3=Daniel S. |last4=Harpole |first4=W. Her main approaches include observational studies, manipulative experiments, and statistical modelling. 

=== Career ===
After her PhD and during her first postdoc, Janneke worked at another LTER site, the [[Cedar Creek Ecosystem Science Reserve]], associated with the [[University of Minnesota]], together with [[G. David Tilman|David Tilman]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=HRL Lab: people |url=https://faculty.washington.edu/jhrl/People.html |access-date=2023-11-28 |website=faculty.washington.edu}}</ref> There she focused on how declining diversity and species identity influences productivity and the impacts of global change on seed production. She then moved on to a postdoc at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara|University of California]], Santa Barbara where she worked with Jonathan Levine and focused on the factors that allowed Mediterranean annual grasses to dominate over the diverse California annual grasses and forbs as well as on the contributions of niche and neutral processes to the coexistence of Serpentine annuals. For that research she was awarded $77,264 from the U.S. NSF Ecology Panel Award.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jonathan |first=Levine |date=2019-11-11 |title=CV of Dr. Jonathan M. Levine |url=https://levine.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/702/2019/11/CV_Levine_11-11-19.pdf}}{{psc|date=December 2023}}</ref> She came to [[University of Washington]] at 2006, received tenure in 2010 and became a full professor in 2014. She was elected a Fellow of [[Ecological Society of America]] in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-03-01 |title=Ecological Society of America announces 2018 Fellows |url=https://esa.org/blog/2018/03/01/ecological-society-of-america-announces-2018-fellows/ |access-date=2025-08-12 |website=Ecological Society of America}}</ref> 

=== MeadoWatch program ===
A program that has been founded in collaboration between the Hille Ris Lambers Lab and Brosi Lab created in 2013 actively engages the public to participate in community science and collect data to better understand the impact of climate change on biodiversity.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About |url=http://www.meadowatch.org/about.html |access-date=2024-01-11 |website=MeadoWatch |language=en}}</ref>
